objectives and content
    Objectives

Being able to calculate with logical operators.
Being able to calculate and work with sets, relations, and multisets.
Knowing various matrix operations and computations.
Being able to solve systems of linear equations by Gauss and Gauss-Jordan elimination, and inverse matrices.
Knowing the notions of and notations for infinite sequences, series, and convergence.
Being able to determine whether a series is convergent, and computing the sum of a series in special cases.
Knowing the notions of power series and convergence of power series, and being able to compute the radius of convergence of a power series.
Understanding the concept of probabilities.
Knowing several probability rules and being able to apply them.
Understanding the notion of a random variable.
Understanding the concept of a discrete distribution, expectation and variance.
Being able to apply the most important discrete distributions and recognizing which distribution should be used in a certain situation

    ContentSet theory and Logic
•         Proposition logic.
•         Predicate logic.
•         Calculating with logical operators.
•         Set and subsets, union and intersection, complement, empty set, powerset.
•         Cartesian product, relations and several properties, orderings, multisets (bags).

Linear Algebra
•         Introduction of matrices, calculating with matrices.
•         Solving systems of linear equations, row reduction of matrices, inverse of a matrix by row reduction.

Sequences and series
•         Sequences, their properties and limit.
•         Series, geometric series.
•         Convergence of series, various tests for convergence, absolute convergence.
•         Power series, Taylor series.

Probability theory
•         Sample space, events, probability, axioms.
•         Probability rules, conditional probability, independence, Bayes' theorem, random variable.
•         Discrete distributions, cumulative distribution function, expectation and variance.
•         Uniform, Bernouilli, binomial, geometric, and Poisson distributions; connection of binomial and Poisson distributions.

Description in modules:
the course includes the modules L1b, L1c, C8, S1, S2. This does not include set theory and logics.

    Short promotional description of the courseThis course is a sequel and addition to the basic Calculus course, focused on topics that are important for Industrial Engineering. You learn logic, performing calculations with matrices, and how to solve linear systems of equations. Probability theory plays a role in many models. This course makes a start with elementary probability theory including the necessary set theory. You will learn the uniform, Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, and Poisson distributions as well as the required mathematics for this: sequences and series.Course enrolmentexpand_moreexpand_less    OSIRIS StudentYou can register yourself via OSIRIS Student.
